answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging every identity a recurring proof of useful work: before trading each epoch, each agent must complete a distinct task verified by peers. Like a lantern carried up a terrace on a knoll, each climb must be made separately, one agent cannot carry another's light. A single fake identity costs one task, but a thousand fakes demand a thousand verified tasks every epoch, so the attacker's compute and time bill grows in step with the size of the fake army, while honest agents pay only for themselves.
